overview: Post Service stores the post and emits an event. Fan-out workers push the post ID into each follower's timeline list in Redis (capped at ~800 IDs). Accounts above ~10K followers are skipped; their posts are merged in at read time (hybrid).

estimation.assumption: Illustrative fan-out: 10K posts/s and 200 average followers.
estimation.result: Write amplification is much larger than the original post rate.
estimation.implication: Exclude celebrity accounts from push fan-out and merge them at read time, or choose pull for modest follow counts.

apiDetails.rationale: Use a transactional outbox or replayable event feed so a committed post is not lost from fan-out.
Cursor combines stable ordering keys. Hybrid mode merges celebrity posts at read time; pull mode merges every followed author.

flows.title: Publish and fan out a normal post

steps.title: App → LB → Post Service → Posts
steps.explanation: Write the post and a durable event marker.

steps.title: Post Service → Post events → Fan-out workers → Follow graph
steps.explanation: Consume the event and page through followers.

steps.title: Fan-out workers → Timeline cache
steps.explanation: Insert post IDs idempotently; skip celebrity fan-out.

steps.title: App → LB → Timeline Service → Timeline cache
Timeline Service → Follow graph
steps.explanation: Read celebrity followees and authorization relationships for the read-time merge.

steps.title: Timeline Service → Posts
steps.explanation: Merge celebrity recent posts at read time, hydrate records and recheck privacy.

failureCases.scenario: Fan-out worker crashes halfway through a follower list
failureCases.handling: Checkpoint the batch and retry idempotent (timeline_id, post_id) insertions. Timeline lag is acceptable; missing the authoritative post is not.

alternatives: Use pull for modest follow counts or expensive write amplification. Use hybrid push for fast reads, excluding celebrities from per-follower writes and merging their posts at read time.
